Graziani (2024, 'Time Series Reversal: An End-of-the-Month Perspective', SSRN/job-market-paper PDF, csef.it) defines the end-of-month reversal signal as the S&P 500 return from the 4th Friday's close to the month-end close (rw=4,t) and the simple rule-of-thumb strategy (TSR: buy next month iff rw=4,t<0) outperforms buy-and-hold over a 45-year window (Jan 1975-Dec 2019 main sample, extended to Dec 1950-Dec 2023 as a robustness check). Its own robustness appendix (A.1.4) tests using the return from 1, 2, or 3 weeks before month-end (rw=1..3) instead of the 4th-Friday week and finds only the last week (rw=4) and daily returns within it (t-4..t-1) have predictive power -- 2-3 week-earlier formation windows do not. Section 2.4 reports a magnitude/precision-scaled variant (TSR-TV, weight = 1-month-ahead forecast / trailing quarterly variance, weight in [-1,2]) with Sharpe 0.588 vs. the simple TSR's 0.384 and S&P's 0.308 (Apr 1986-Dec 2019); trading-cost appendix A.1.3 finds breakeven cost ~16bp/transaction vs. typical index costs of 3-9bp/yr. Section 2.5 replicates on DOW (pattern holds) and Russell 2000 (no clear pattern); QQQ/Nasdaq-100 is not tested in the paper.
